blocks.orig: Lake Natron is a salt or soda lake not far from Lake Manyara in northern Tanzania. It is located in the Gregory Rift, the eastern branch of the East African Rift. The lake lays at the foot of the Ol Doinyo Lengai, an active volcano.
blocks.html: In northern Tanzania, not far from Lake Manyara, lies Lake Natron, a salt or soda lake. It sits in the Gregory Rift, which forms the eastern branch of the East African Rift, right at the foot of Ol Doinyo Lengai, an active volcano.

blocks.orig: Lake Natron is quite shallow, less than three meters deep, and varies in width depending on its water level. The lake is 57 kilometers long and 22 kilometers wide. The area receives irregular seasonal rainfall, mainly between December and May. The temperatures at the lake are often over 40 °C.
blocks.html: The lake is fairly shallow, under three metres deep, and its width changes with the water level. Lake Natron measures 57 kilometres in length and 22 kilometres across. Rain here is seasonal and unpredictable, falling mostly between December and May, and temperatures by the lake frequently climb above 40 °C.

blocks.orig: As the fresh water evaporates in the lake, water with high concentrations of salt minerals such as sodium and trona remains. The alkalinity of the lake can reach a pH level of more than 12. Special bacteria and blue algae thrive in this environment and form an ideal breeding ground for the life of birds. Such halophilic organisms include some cyano bacteria that, like plants, produce their own food through photosynthesis. The red pigment in those cyano bacteria produces the deep red colors of the lake’s waters and the orange colors in the shallow areas. Salt-loving microorganisms living there are coloring the alkali salt crust on the surface of the lake is red or pink.
blocks.html: When the fresh water in the lake evaporates, what stays behind is water heavily loaded with salt minerals such as sodium and trona. The lake's alkalinity can exceed a pH of 12. Specialised bacteria and blue algae do well in these conditions and create an ideal feeding and breeding ground for birds. These salt-tolerant organisms include certain cyano bacteria that make their own food through photosynthesis, just as plants do. The red pigment in those cyano bacteria gives the lake its deep red water and the orange tints in the shallows. The salt-loving microorganisms living here also colour the alkali salt crust on the lake's surface red or pink.

blocks.orig: Lake Natron, the perfect breeding place for Flamingos
blocks.html: Lake Natron, the ideal flamingo breeding ground

blocks.orig: Flamingos find a safe breeding ground at Lake Natron, since most other animals find its caustic environment and high temperature of the lake (up to 60 °C) as well as its high salinity inhospitable. It therefore provides a good barrier against predators trying to reach nests on seasonal evaporation islands. Every year, more than two million flamingos come here to lay their eggs and chicks hatch between September and April. Cyanobacteria are increasing with the salinity of the water, and the lake can carry more nests. Larger flamingos also breed in the Wadden Sea.
blocks.html: At Lake Natron flamingos can breed in safety, because the lake's caustic water, high temperature (up to 60 °C) and strong salinity keep most other animals away. This creates an effective barrier against predators that might otherwise reach the nests on the seasonal evaporation islands. Each year more than two million flamingos arrive here to lay their eggs, and the chicks hatch between September and April. As the water grows saltier, cyanobacteria multiply and the lake can support more nests. Larger flamingos also breed in the Wadden Sea.

blocks.orig: Some fish species (such as tilapia) can survive in the slightly less salty water near the shore. Lake Natron is also home to some endemic algae, invertebrates and other birds. Tens of thousands of other birds can be spotted near the lake, making Lake Natron a prime destination for bird lovers in Africa.
blocks.html: Certain fish, tilapia among them, manage to live in the slightly less salty water close to the shore. Lake Natron also supports some endemic algae, invertebrates and other birds. Tens of thousands of other birds can be seen around the lake, which makes Lake Natron one of Africa's top destinations for bird lovers.

blocks.orig: Lake Natron is also well-connected to other National parks, such as: Lake Manyara, the Ngorongoro Conservation Area in the south and the Northern Serengeti National Park in the west. Usually Lake Natron will be visited after Lake Manyara National Park.
blocks.html: Lake Natron also links well with other national parks, including Lake Manyara, the Ngorongoro Conservation Area to the south and the Northern Serengeti National Park to the west. Most travellers visit Lake Natron after Lake Manyara National Park.

blocks.orig: My name is Bosco and I’m already bringing visitors to Lake Natron for over 20 years. Natron is a well appreciated place by our guests. This is also because it is different from all other game drives and it gives people the chance to stretch the legs, and do some other activities before continue with safari. From the end of July we often go from Lake Natron to Northern Serengeti to see the river crossings.
blocks.html: I'm Bosco, and I have been taking visitors to Lake Natron for more than 20 years now. Our guests really value Natron, partly because it is unlike any other game drive: it gives people a chance to stretch their legs and try a few other activities before carrying on with the safari. From the end of July onwards we often travel from Lake Natron to the Northern Serengeti for the river crossings.

blocks.orig: How long to stay? Not less than 2 nights.
blocks.html: How long should you stay? At least 2 nights.

blocks.orig: Which accommodation? Maasai Giraffe Eco Camp for the more budget one and Lake Natron Camp for the more luxurious guests.
blocks.html: Where to stay? Maasai Giraffe Eco Camp if you are on a tighter budget, and Lake Natron Camp for guests who want more luxury.

blocks.orig: It is hard to predict when the flamingos are in Lake Natron, especially the last years it has changed a bit, and it all depends on the rainfall. The problem with Lake Natron is that you have to avoid it in the more wet seasons, because there is a very high chance that your car gets stuck in the mud. Therefore, from July – October are the best time to reach Lake Natron by car.
blocks.html: Predicting when the flamingos will be at Lake Natron is difficult; in recent years the pattern has shifted somewhat, and everything hinges on the rainfall. The catch with Lake Natron is that you need to stay away in the wetter seasons, as there is a very real chance of your car getting stuck in the mud. For that reason July – October is the best time to reach Lake Natron by car.
